question.problem:
Consider the following polynomials:

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=-1-t+2{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=t-{t}^{2},\,q(t)=3-3t.
$$

If $B=\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\},$ and $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
question.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(-1-t+2{t}^{2})+{x}_{2}(t-{t}^{2}) & =3-3t \\ -{x}_{1}+(-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2})t+(2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}){t}^{2} & =3-3t.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}=3 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-3 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & -1 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}=3 \\ {x}_{2}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

From the first and second equations, we get ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=-6.$ 

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -6\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-3+(-6)=-9.$
